##### Business rules & calculations

- **[I]** Positions are event-sourced from trades, fills, settlements, corporate actions, cash movements and approved valuations; external custody evidence reconciles to the book and never overwrites it.
- **[I]** Quantity = settled quantity ± unsettled quantity; available-to-trade = settled quantity − pending sales − reservations; private assets are shown "Restricted".
- **[O]** The T-bill row follows the availability rule: 5,200,000 settled − 660,000 pending sale = 4,540,000 available. The Econet row follows the quantity rule: 708,000 settled − 80,000 pending sale = 628,000.
- **[O]** Row state *Review* corresponds to an open custodian difference (ZIM.VX), matched by the book-health item *Custodian difference* and by KPI *Exceptions*.
- **[O]** Filters combine with AND (see Tables).
- BR-055: Position quantity must equal settled + unsettled quantity, and the Position count, Market value and Available cash KPIs must equal the aggregates of the positions in scope **[P]**.
- BR-056: A position whose custodian quantity differs from the IBOR quantity is shown as *Review* and appears in the Exceptions count until the break is resolved; the reconciliation tab shows the actual difference **[P]**.
- BR-057: Historical snapshots are read-only reconstructions from effective-time records; they never change current positions **[P]**.
- Existing FR-PORT-003 and FR-PORT-004 apply (as-of snapshots; ladder T..T+3 sums per day equal pending settlements).

##### Edge cases

- **[O]** *Reconcile positions* shows its success toast even when the role cannot open Operations Control.
- **[O]** *Refresh IBOR* changes nothing visible except re-rendering the table; the as-of time and KPIs stay fixed.
- **[O]** The "IBOR current" chip, KPIs and control bar ignore filters and Review rows.
- **[O]** The ladder mixes currencies (T+3 in ZWG) with no base-currency total.
- **[O]** The Lots, Reconciliation and History tabs show the same content for every position, so a Treasury bill or the private asset shows equity lots.
- **[O]** The Position ledger tab can only be opened for the eight listed positions; a stale id falls back to DLTA.ZW.
- **[O]** The NAV & Valuation source preview "IBOR Position Snapshot" shows different quantities (DLTA 482,440; INN 214,300) from this page; it is a separate fund-level fixture.
- **[I]** A search for an ISIN returns no rows.
- **[I]** A portfolio with thousands of positions is not supported by the client-side filter.

##### Gaps, defects & open questions

- **DEF-206** Search placeholder promises ISIN search but ISIN is neither in the data nor searched.
- **DEF-207** *Historical snapshot* has no date input; *Columns* has no selector; both are descriptive text only.
- **DEF-208** *Reconcile positions* goes to Operations Control rather than Reconciliations and shows its success toast when navigation is denied.
- **DEF-209** *Refresh IBOR* is a local re-render, not a job; as-of and KPIs do not update.
- **DEF-210** Quantity does not equal settled plus unsettled for DLTA.ZW, INN.ZW and ZIM.VX (quantity equals settled while unsettled is non-zero); USD-CASH shows quantity 7,000 against value US$ 10,000; USD-CASH available ignores its -3,000 unsettled.
- **DEF-211** Lots, Reconciliation and History tabs are hard-coded to DLTA.ZW data for all positions; the Break value is always 0 even for ZIM.VX in Review.
- **DEF-212** KPIs (US$ 84.62M, 438 positions) do not match the eight-row table (about US$ 16.85M).
- **DEF-213** All values are display strings, so no sorting or totals are possible.
- **DEF-214** Sidebar badge "4" and the Exceptions KPI are static.
- **DEF-215** *Trade security* does not pre-select the security on the Order Management page.
- FR-IBOR-002: Position list from `GET /api/v1/ibor/positions` with server-side search (ticker, name, portfolio, asset class, ISIN), filters, sorting and paging — AC: a 50 000-position book returns the first page in the response-time target of section 8.1; filters AND-combine; the count label shows the total matching rows.
- FR-IBOR-003: As-of snapshot — AC: choosing a past timestamp returns the positions, cash, unsettled activity and prices at that time, and the page is labelled as a historical view.
- FR-IBOR-004: *Refresh IBOR* as an asynchronous job with visible status — AC: the button shows queued / running / complete / failed; on completion the table, KPIs, as-of and ladder reload; an operations permission is required.
- FR-IBOR-005: KPI tiles and chip computed from the position aggregates — AC: Positions, Market value, Available cash, Unsettled buys, Accrued income and Exceptions equal the aggregates of the data in scope.
- FR-IBOR-006: Position detail with real tax lots, reconciliation difference and event history per position — AC: the Lots tab quantities sum to the position quantity; the Reconciliation tab shows the actual custodian difference; the History tab lists the sequenced events for that position.
- FR-IBOR-007: Column chooser — AC: selected column groups persist per user and the table shows exactly the chosen groups.
- FR-IBOR-008: Settlement ladder in base currency with a currency breakdown — AC: each bucket total equals the sum of pending settlements for that date.
- Q-62: Which permission and roles may refresh the IBOR and start a holdings reconciliation? — default: `operations.view` holders (Operations, Dealer, Fund Accountant, Compliance, Auditor read-only), matching the proposed `POST /ibor/refresh` gate.
- Q-63: Should position quantities be shown as numbers with currency columns rather than preformatted strings? — default: yes; numeric fields with formatting in the UI.
- Q-64: Source for the "Last event" and "Processing lag" values — default: the position-event stream metadata.

Without it the sidebar entry is hidden (display none) and `navigate('cash')` shows the toast "Access restricted" with message "<Role label> does not have permission to open this workspace." (error) and does not navigate; if the user is already on the page when their role changes, they are redirected to the first visible sidebar entry. [O] |

##### Layout

1. Page head: eyebrow "CLIENT CASH · IMMUTABLE SUBLEDGER · RESERVATIONS · EXTERNAL EVIDENCE"; title *Cash & Ledgers*; copy (final, after V16) "Cash ownership, reservations and forecasts."; page actions *Explain balance*, *Import statement*, *New journal*.
2. Context bar (6 cells): *Client*, *Portfolio*, *Cash account*, *Currency*, *As of*, freshness indicator.
3. Cash-state tile grid (6 tiles, 6 columns; 3 columns at 1200 px and below, 2 at 980 px and below, 1 at 640 px and below).
4. *Available cash proof* card.
5. Tab strip (role "tablist", aria-label "Cash control workspaces"): *Cash Ledger* (default active), *Reservations*, *Expected Cash*, *Statement Imports*.
6. Tab panel *Cash Ledger*: card head with *Trace source* and *New controlled journal*; ledger control strip (5 cells); journal table.
7. Tab panel *Reservations*: card head with *New reservation*; reservation table.
8. Tab panel *Expected Cash*: card head with *Add expected movement*; expectation table.
9. Tab panel *Statement Imports*: card head with *Upload external statement*; import-control grid (4 tiles); statement-import table.
10. Overlays: drawer (right side) used for Explain, journal, reservation, statement import, new journal, new reservation and new expected movement; toast stack.

Only the active tab panel is displayed. [O]

##### Inputs & validation

All form fields live in drawers; they are specified under *Modals & drawers*. Page-level inputs (context bar) are specified under *Elements* (rows 4 to 8) and are non-functional. Shared decimal rule used by every amount field handled by the shared parser (journal debit/credit, reservation amount): the value has commas removed and surrounding spaces trimmed, then must match an optional sign, one or more digits and optionally a decimal point with zero to two digits. Anything else is rejected with "Use a decimal amount with up to 2 places." Accepted examples: "1,000", "+5", "5."; rejected examples: ".50", "1.234", "abc". Amounts are held as integer minor units (BigInt) so comparisons are exact. [O]

##### States

- Empty: each of the four tables renders an empty body with no message; no illustration or call to action. [O]
- Loading: none; data is synchronous and in memory. In live mode the legacy scripts wait for the bridge's initial load (with a timeout) before the page is evaluated; there is no spinner or skeleton. [O]
- Error: toasts only (type error, auto-dismiss after 3.6 s); there are no inline field errors, no banners and no retry controls. If the API is unreachable or the user is signed out, the page silently uses the prototype demo data. [O]
- Disabled / read-only: RBAC-disabled buttons are shown at reduced opacity with the not-allowed cursor and tooltip "Not permitted for <Role label>". POSTED journals offer only *Create reversal*; COMMITTED and REJECTED batches offer no actions; CONSUMED and RELEASED reservations offer only *Trace source*. The `auditor` role sees everything but all five statically gated buttons are disabled; drawer buttons stay clickable and fail at click time where a check exists (journal approve, reversal, reservation release, statement commit); statement validate/submit/reject, journal reject and the expectation form have no check at all. [O]
- Conditional: *Release remainder* appears only for ACTIVE and PARTIALLY_CONSUMED reservations; drawer buttons depend on status as listed above; the journal drawer balance line shows "✓ Balanced journal" or "× UNBALANCED — posting blocked"; the page redirects away when the role loses `cash.view`; on viewports of 1200 px and below the context bar and tiles collapse to 3 columns, at 980 px and below to 2 columns (ledger strip also 2), at 640 px and below to 1 column; in Focus mode (browser key `matanhoFocus` not "off") the page copy is the short text and non-primary sidebar items are collapsed. [O]

##### Journal state machine (as implemented)

```
(new draft or reversal) -> PENDING_APPROVAL
PENDING_APPROVAL -- Approve & post (cash.journal.approve; maker differs from user; total debit = total credit) --> POSTED
PENDING_APPROVAL -- Reject --> (toast only; no state change)
POSTED -- Create reversal (cash.journal.create) --> new REV-... journal in PENDING_APPROVAL (original unchanged)
```

[O]. Implied but not implemented: separate DRAFT step before PENDING_APPROVAL, REJECTED with reason, withdraw/cancel, linked corrected journal, "reversed by" link on the original. [I]

##### Reservation state machine (as implemented)

```
(create) -> ACTIVE
ACTIVE -- settlement consumes part --> PARTIALLY_CONSUMED -- settlement consumes rest --> CONSUMED
ACTIVE or PARTIALLY_CONSUMED -- Release remainder (cash.reservation) --> RELEASED (remaining 0.00)
```

Create and Release are [O]; consumption by settlement exists only in seed data [I]; automatic expiry at the *Expiry* date is not implemented [I].

##### Statement import state machine (as implemented)

```
(upload) RECEIVED -- Validate staging --> VALIDATED -- Submit for approval --> PENDING_APPROVAL
PENDING_APPROVAL -- Commit evidence (cash.import; maker differs from user) --> COMMITTED (immutable)
PENDING_APPROVAL -- Reject batch --> REJECTED (immutable)
```

[O]. Implied but not implemented: validation failure state, tolerance breach blocking, re-upload of a corrected version, explicit "warnings acknowledged" step. [I]

##### Order-ticket cash availability check (related; lives on Orders, not on this page)

Documented here because FR-OMS-003, FR-OMS-005 and FR-CASH-005 depend on it. [O]

- Balance source: a hard-coded map per portfolio and currency, not the cash page and not the account list. Balanced Growth Fund USD 1,862,400 ("CBZ USD Operating · •••• 4208") and ZWG 18,460,000 ("CBZ ZWG Operating · •••• 7731"); USD Equity Fund USD 3,240,000 ("Stanbic USD Dealing · •••• 9814") and ZWG 0 ("No active ZWG dealing account"); Income Fund USD 2,780,000 ("FBC USD Income · •••• 3146") and ZWG 12,900,000 ("FBC ZWG Income · •••• 5052"); Zimbabwe Opportunities USD 940,000 ("NMB USD Dealing · •••• 1149") and ZWG 26,750,000 ("NMB ZWG Dealing · •••• 6654"). Any other portfolio/currency pair: balance 0 and account text "No <ccy> dealing account configured". Wiring: Prototype. [O]
- Formula: gross = quantity × price; fees = gross × 0.65 % (constant 0.0065); Buy: after = balance − (gross + fees); Sell: after = balance + gross − fees. [O]
- State: *fail* when after < 0; *warn* when balance > 0 and after ÷ balance < 0.15; otherwise *good*. [O]
- Panel (final, V56): section "DEALING ACCOUNT" with the account text and caption "IBOR cash ledger · live order estimate"; tiles *Available now* (portfolio name), *Trade cash required* (Buy, "− <amount>") or *Expected proceeds* (Sell, "+ <amount>"), with "<quantity> shares × <price>", and *Available after trade* with caption "Insufficient available cash" (fail), "Low residual cash" (warn) or "Estimated post-trade cash" (good); meta lines "Estimated dealing costs 0.65% · <fees>" and "Updates instantly with side, quantity, price, portfolio and security." The earlier V54 panel "Cash available for this trade" (caption "IBOR cash ledger · controlled balance", with a cost-buffer note and a progress bar) is hidden by a V56 style rule. [O]; V54 panel superseded.
- Control row "Cash / position availability": badge *Fail* / *Review* / *Pass*; caption "Order exceeds available dealing cash" (Buy, fail), "Cash after order <amount>" (Buy, otherwise) or "Estimated cash after sale <amount>" (Sell). [O]
- Hard block: on *Validate* or *Submit*, a Buy whose *after* is negative is stopped by the V54 listener before V56 runs: toast "Insufficient available cash" — "<portfolio> would be <ccy amount> short after this order. Reduce the quantity or select another portfolio." (error). V56's own check ("Pre-trade check failed" — "available cash shortfall <amount>") is therefore pre-empted. A participation above 25 % of average daily volume produces only a review note, not a block. [O]
- Confirmation dialog shows *Cash before* and *Cash after*. Submitting an order stores it in browser keys `matanho-v56-submitted-orders` and `matanho-v53-submitted-orders` only; it does **not** create a cash reservation and does not link to the cash page. [O]

##### Business rules & calculations

- Availability: available = max(0, posted settled + reusable cleared proceeds / approved credit − active reservations − holds − pending withdrawals − minimum buffer); withdrawable = settled − reservations − holds − buffer; calculation version label "AVAIL-<ccy>-v4"; expected movements are projection only and must not change availability; the external statement balance is reconciliation evidence, never the source of availability. [O] copy and seed data; calculation not implemented (FR-CASH-001, FR-CASH-006).
- Double entry: total debit must equal total credit, compared exactly in integer minor units, at draft creation and again at approval. Amounts allow at most 2 decimals and must be non-negative magnitudes; zero is accepted today. [O] (FR-CASH-002)
- Immutability: no edit or delete control exists for journals in any status; corrections are exact-inverse reversals, one reversal per journal (id "REV-<suffix>"). [O] by UI omission (FR-CASH-003, FR-CASH-004)
- Maker-checker (BR-001): journal approval and statement commit compare the record's maker with the hard-coded name "T. Moyo", the current user for every role, so records created in-session can never be approved or committed, and any seeded record whose maker is not "T. Moyo" can be. Quote: "You cannot approve a journal you created or materially changed." and "The uploader/reviewer cannot commit their own controlled staging version." [O]
- Reservation limit: 0 < amount ≤ 7,000.00 (constant); not decremented by created reservations. [O] (FR-CASH-005)
- Reservation release: only for ACTIVE or PARTIALLY_CONSUMED; sets remaining to 0 and never deletes. [O]
- Import commit: only from PENDING_APPROVAL; claimed gates (mapping, arithmetic tolerance, duplicate checks, frozen staging version) are text only. [O] copy; [I] gates (FR-CASH-007)
- Permission usage on this page: `cash.close` and `cash.approve` are not used by any control; `cash.approve` gates cash-account lifecycle and capital-event approval in the API. The role-permission matrix on the RBAC page lists `cash.view`, `cash.journal.create`, `cash.journal.approve`, `cash.reservation`, `cash.import` and `cash.close` (not `cash.approve`). The SoD scan flags "Cash maker-checker relaxed" when the cash-approval policy is not "independent", and "Platform admin monetary privilege" when `system_admin` holds `cash.journal.create`, `cash.journal.approve` or `cash.close` (BR-002, BR-005); the policy value has no effect on this page. [O]
- Identifier generation: "JRN-260826-" + (count + 40); "REV-" + suffix; "RSV-" + (800 + count); "IMP-260826-" + (21 + count); fixed date prefix 26 Aug 2026. [O]
- Identity: there is no authenticated user identity in the cash engine; maker is "T. Moyo" for all in-session records and the reservation owner is the role label. [O]
- BR-058: Order-eligible available cash is a single server-calculated value shared by the cash page, the order ticket, reservations and withdrawals (rule version recorded with every result).
- BR-059: Journal posting, reservation creation and statement commit are atomic with row-level locking of the cash account so concurrent requests cannot over-reserve or double-post.

##### Edge cases

- A journal's currency is not validated against the cash account's currency; USD and ZWG can be mixed. [O]
- Reversing a posted reversal would produce the id "REV-REV-…" (only "JRN-" is stripped). [O]
- A zero-value journal (0.00 debit and credit) is accepted; a journal is always stored as an outflow on the cash line regardless of purpose. [O]
- Value date, required date and expiry are free text; "Required / expiry" in the reservation form is ignored. [O]
- If the API returns an empty cash-account list in live mode, the empty list is used (it is not replaced by the seed), so *Explain* finds no account and fails without opening a drawer; the seeded database creates no cash accounts. [O] by code reading
- In live mode without account "CCA-1001", every *Explain* opens the first account of the list, which differs from the static tiles. [O]
- Hard-coded context currency default is ZWG while all figures are USD. [O]
- The Accounting-queue link to JRN-260826-032 navigates to the page without opening that journal. [O]
- The tile button text "3 reservations" and "4 movements" are static and do not follow created records. [O]
- Uploading two files in the same session yields ids IMP-260826-24 and IMP-260826-25; ids are count-based and would collide if rows could be removed (they cannot). [O]

##### Gaps, defects & open questions

- **DEF-216** The context bar (client, portfolio, cash account, currency) has no listeners; no figure or table responds, and the currency defaults to ZWG while all values are USD.
- **DEF-217** All six tiles, the *Available cash proof* card and the ledger control strip are static markup for CCA-1001; they are not recomputed after approving a journal, creating a reservation or committing a statement.
- **DEF-218** The ledger control strip contradicts the seed (posted outflows 480.00 although POSTED journal JRN-260826-031 is −3,005.00; closing 10,000.00 versus committed statement closing 9,995.00); EXPECTED NET +480.00 does not equal the sum of the four expectation rows.
- **DEF-219** Seed account CCA-1042 subtracts an expected outflow (−52,000.00) in *available*, and CCA-1188 *withdrawable* is 25,000.00 below *available* with no stated reason.
- **DEF-220** *Explain* subtotal shows the stored available value instead of computing it from the displayed lines; *Reproduce number* therefore does not reproduce anything.
- **DEF-221** *Trace source* in the ledger card opens the balance explanation, not a source trace; *Trace source* in the reservation drawer is a toast only.
- **DEF-222** Maker-checker compares against the literal "T. Moyo" instead of the authenticated user; in-session drafts, reversals and uploads can never be approved or committed, and BR-001 is not enforced against real users.
- **DEF-223** Journal *Reject* is a toast only (no state, no reason, drawer stays open); statement *Validate staging*, *Submit for approval* and *Reject batch* have no permission check; *Add expected movement* has no permission gate.
- **DEF-224** The balance line in the journal drawer is styled green even for "× UNBALANCED — posting blocked".
- **DEF-225** Reservation availability is the constant 7,000.00 and is not reduced by created reservations; the "Required / expiry" field is ignored; the account and currency are fixed to CCA-1001 / USD.
- **DEF-226** New journals are always recorded as an outflow; the *Reason* field is not saved; only two lines can be entered; a zero amount passes; currency is not checked against the account.
- **DEF-227** V8 expectation form creates nothing (toast only) and lists accounts in every status.
- **DEF-228** Statement upload does not read or parse the file; *Validate staging* always passes; the commit gates and the four control tiles are text only; REJECTED is shown with the blue (not red) badge.
- **DEF-229** The same permission `cash.import` authorises uploading and committing; the maker-checker split relies only on the name check.
- **DEF-230** The orphan `period-close-precheck` handler is unreachable; no close day/period control exists, so `cash.close` has no effect.
- **DEF-231** The order ticket's cash check uses its own hard-coded balances (e.g. Balanced Growth Fund USD 1,862,400) that contradict the cash page (US$ 7,000.00 for the same portfolio's account), applies a fixed 0.65 % cost buffer, creates no reservation on submit and has no link to the cash page.
- **DEF-232** The sidebar badge "3" on *Cash* is static; the page copy replacement by Focus mode hides the original description permanently.
- FR-CASH-009: The context bar filters balances, tiles, proof card and all four tables by client, portfolio, cash account and currency, and the *As of* control reconstructs balances at a past time — AC: changing any selector refreshes every number from `GET /api/v1/cash/balances` within 2 seconds and an as-of in the past reproduces the figures reported at that time.
- FR-CASH-010: Each tile's *Explain* shows the exact journals, reservations, holds and policy lines contributing to that state, and the available figure equals the displayed formula — AC: for every state the sum of displayed contributing lines equals the tile value to the minor unit.
- FR-CASH-011: Journal entry supports two or more lines, a mandatory reason and evidence reference, value date picker, currency locked to the account currency, amount greater than 0, and records direction from the lines instead of always as an outflow — AC: a three-line journal that balances is accepted; a journal with currency different from the account is rejected with 400.
- FR-CASH-012: Journal *Reject* requires a reason and moves the journal to REJECTED with an audit entry — AC: rejecting without a reason returns 400; the rejected journal is read-only and shows the reason.
- FR-CASH-013: Maker-checker for journals, reversals, reservations released on behalf of others, account lifecycle and statement commits is enforced on the authenticated user id — AC: the same user approving their own journal or committing their own import receives 403 `sod_violation`.
- FR-CASH-014: Reservation creation checks live available cash atomically, saves account, currency, required date and expiry, and updates all tiles — AC: two concurrent reservations that together exceed available cash result in exactly one success and one 409.
- FR-CASH-015: Submitting a buy order creates a linked cash reservation and the order ticket reads availability from the same service as the cash page — AC: after submission the cash page RESERVED tile increases by notional plus estimated fees and the ticket shows the same available figure as the cash page for that account.
- FR-CASH-016: Expected movements are persisted, gated by `cash.journal.create`, listed in the table and transition EXPECTED → DUE → POSTED when the linked journal posts — AC: creating an expectation adds a row and changes only EXPECTED NET.
- FR-CASH-017: Statement import parses CAMT.053 and CSV, maps the account and currency, normalises signs (positive = Matanho cash increased), checks opening + movements = closing within the account's tolerance profile, rejects duplicate file hash, statement and line, and freezes the reviewed staging version before commit — AC: a file whose arithmetic is outside tolerance cannot reach PENDING_APPROVAL; re-uploading the same file returns 409.
- FR-CASH-018: A close day / close period control with a blockers pre-check (statement coverage, balance variance, suspense, aged open items, sub-ledger-to-GL, checker approval) available to `cash.close` holders — AC: close is refused with every blocker itemised until all pass; after close a journal dated in the period returns 409.
- FR-CASH-019: Table filters, search and column sort on all four tabs, an empty-state message, and keyboard-accessible tabs with `aria-selected` — AC: each tab filters by status and account and shows "No records" when empty.
- BR-060: A cash account in status SUSPENDED, CLOSING or CLOSED accepts no new reservations or manual journals; reconciliation postings remain allowed.
- Q-65: Is a separate permission needed for committing statement imports (checker) distinct from uploading them (maker)? — default: statement commit requires `cash.journal.approve` and the maker may not commit.
- Q-66: Should `cash.approve` (held by `investment_director` and `compliance`) gate any cash-ledger action, or only cash-account lifecycle and capital-event approval? — default: only account lifecycle and capital events.
- Q-67: Should expected movements be creatable by roles that cannot post journals (for example `portfolio_manager`, `dealer`)? — default: only holders of `cash.journal.create`.
- Q-68: Are minimum buffer and pending-withdrawal amounts configured per account (tolerance profile) or per portfolio mandate? — default: per cash account, versioned with the availability rule.
- Q-69: Which cash accounts feed order-ticket availability when a portfolio has several accounts in one currency? — default: sum of ACTIVE accounts of that portfolio and currency.

##### Tables

**Runbook (task list)** — rendered as a list of grid rows (`.v36-ops-task`), not an HTML table. Grid columns `62px | 8px | 1fr | auto` (at 760 px and below: `52px | 7px | 1fr`, with the state label moved under the text).

| Column | Format | Sortable | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Time | `HH:MM` 24-hour (CAT), or the literal *Now* for manually added tasks; 10 px bold | No | Operational deadline. No overdue calculation, no clock comparison: the 15:50 task is never flagged late. **[O]** |
| Status dot | 7 px circle | No | Colour by state: *Due* amber `#d58b1d`; *Blocked* red `#d83c54`; *Scheduled* blue `#3158e8`. **[O]** |
| Task | Line 1 bold: "<Area> · <Title>"; line 2 small grey: "<Dependency> · owner <Owner>" (all HTML-escaped) | No | **[O]** |
| State | Plain grey text `#6b798c` (*Due* / *Blocked* / *Scheduled*), no pill | No | V33 rendered a chip: *Blocked* red/fail, *Due* amber/warn, other blue/info. **[O]** (superseded) |

- **Seed tasks** (tuple = time, area, title, state, dependency, owner) **[O]**, Prototype wiring:

| # | Time | Area | Title | State | Dependency | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 15:50 | Settlement | Resolve Zimplats VFEX settlement fail | Due | Reconciliations dependency | T. Moyo |
| 2 | 16:00 | Cash | Fund Growth Equity IV capital call | Due | Treasury approval | N. Dube |
| 3 | 16:15 | Corporate actions | Elect on Delta scrip / cash event | Due | PM instruction | S. Moyo |
| 4 | 16:30 | Valuation | Review private asset price exception | Blocked | Current valuation statement | Fund Accounting |
| 5 | 17:00 | Close | Prepare NAV close readiness | Blocked | Recon + valuation | N. Dube |
| 6 | 17:20 | Reporting | Publish client PBOR snapshot | Scheduled | NAV release | Client Services |
| 7 | 17:30 | Settlement | Confirm broker allocations | Scheduled | Execution complete | T. Moyo |
| + | Now | Manual | New controlled operations task | Due | Manual dependency review | Current operator |

  The last row is prepended each time *+ Operations task* is pressed. Counts: *All* 7, *Due* 3, *Blocked* 2, *Scheduled* 2. The V33 seed had tasks 1-6 only, without an owner, with titles "Resolve Zimplats VFEX fail" and "Elect on Delta scrip/cash event", and manual-task dependency "Assigned to current operator". **[O]**
- **Filters**: single-select, exact string equality on the state: *All* = every task; *Due* = state is "Due"; *Blocked* = state is "Blocked"; *Scheduled* = state is "Scheduled". Clicking a chip moves the active highlight to that chip only and re-renders. The filter is held in memory and resets to *All* on reload. **[O]**
- **Search**: none. **Sort**: none; order is array order (hard-coded chronological; manual tasks prepended; never re-sorted). **Pagination**: none. **Owner/area filter**: none. **[O]**
- **Row click**: opens the *Task detail* modal (below) for the clicked task; the index is resolved against the filtered list, so it stays correct under filtering. Hover background `#fafcff`, cursor pointer. **[O]** (V33: row click only showed the toast "Operations task" with the task title.)
- **Row actions**: none. There is no *Mark done*, *Mark blocked*, note entry, reassign, reschedule, evidence upload or delete in the row or in the modal. **[O]**
- **Status values → colour**: *Due* amber, *Blocked* red, *Scheduled* blue (dot only). No *Done* / *Completed* state exists in the task list. **[O]**
- **Empty result** for a filter: the list is cleared with no message (not reachable with seed data because every filter has at least two rows). **[O]**

##### States

- Empty: filter with no matching tasks leaves the runbook blank with no message **[O]**; target text "No tasks match this filter." **[P]**.
- Loading: none **[O]**. Before V36 builds (about 1.85 s after load) the superseded V33 version of the page is shown and is interactive; before V33 initialises (about 0.55 s) its runbook container is empty. Target: skeleton while `GET /v1/operations/tasks` loads **[P]**.
- Error: none; there is no data fetch **[O]**. Target: inline banner with *Retry* when the tasks or status call fails **[P]**.
- Disabled / read-only: no control is ever disabled or hidden by role **[O]**. A role without `operations.view` cannot open the page (see Access) **[O]**.
- Conditional: toast type is *info*; if the global toast function is missing a local fallback toast fades after 2.7 s **[O]**. Manual tasks created while the V33 version is visible are discarded when V36 rebuilds the page **[O]**. Responsive collapse per Layout **[O]**.

##### Business rules & calculations

- Page access requires `operations.view`; no action-level permission exists in either the in-code role list or the seeded role catalog **[O]**.
- Runbook filter predicate is exact equality on the state string **[O]**.
- Manual task creation always yields time *Now*, area *Manual*, state *Due*, dependency "Manual dependency review", owner "Current operator" (literal text, not the signed-in user's name) **[O]**.
- Tasks are never removed, completed or re-ordered **[O]**.
- All KPI values, dependency percentages, link counts and chart series are literals and are not computed from the task array **[O]**.
- Positioning rule: Reconciliations is an independent control function (matching and break resolution on 5.A.17); Operations owns deadlines, dependencies and hand-offs **[O]**.
- Implied task lifecycle **[I]**: *Scheduled → Due → (Blocked ⇄ Due) → Done*; *Blocked* requires a reason and the blocking dependency; *Done* requires a completion note and evidence; a hand-off updates or creates the downstream owner's task rather than relying on email (copy "Downstream owner receives state, not an email-only instruction").
- Implied dependency chain **[I]**: task 5 *Prepare NAV close readiness* depends on task 1 (reconciliation of the settlement fail) and task 4 (valuation exception); task 6 *Publish client PBOR snapshot* depends on NAV release (5.A.18); task 7 *Confirm broker allocations* depends on execution completion (5.A.5); task 2 depends on Treasury approval; task 3 on PM instruction. Not enforced in code.
- Cut-off times **[I]**: the time column is the operational deadline in CAT; the *Today · CAT* chip states the time zone; there is no overdue or SLA logic.
- BR-061: A task is **overdue** when the current CAT time is later than its deadline and its state is not *Done*; overdue tasks show a red *Overdue* flag and count towards *Due today*.
- BR-062: A task whose dependency is not *Done* cannot be marked *Done*; completing a task re-evaluates dependants and automatically moves *Blocked* tasks whose blockers have cleared to *Due*.
- BR-063: A task creator may not mark their own task *Done* when the task is flagged as a control task (extends BR-001).
- BR-064: KPI and dependency values are computed server-side from live data: *Due today* = tasks due today with state ≠ *Done*; *Close blockers* = tasks and controls with state *Blocked* that gate period close; *Settlement* readiness % = settled or matched instructions ÷ total instructions for today; *Cash* % = share of bank feeds received within their schedule; *Valuation* % = priced positions ÷ total positions; *Accounting* % = completed close-checklist items ÷ total items.

##### Edge cases

- Repeated clicks on *+ Operations task* create identical duplicate tasks (no id, no de-dup) **[O]**.
- When the active filter is *Blocked* or *Scheduled*, the new *Due* task is added but not shown while the toast still says "New task added to today’s runbook." **[O]**
- The new task's time *Now* is not a clock time and the list is not re-sorted, so it sits above 15:50 regardless of the real time **[O]**.
- Users who open Operations within ~1.85 s of load briefly see the V33 version; its *+ Operations task* re-renders with filter *All* without updating the active chip, and its manual tasks are lost when V36 rebuilds **[O]**.
- A role with `operations.view` but without `valuation.view` (dealer) sees *Valuation*, *Accounting* and *Open NAV & Valuation* as ordinary clickable items that only produce the "Access restricted" toast **[O]**.
- The page is built once at boot; later navigation to the page does not rebuild it, so in-memory tasks and the active filter persist until a full reload **[O]**.
- A task detail modal opened for a filtered row resolves the correct task; closing it never changes the filter **[O]**.

##### Gaps, defects & open questions

- **DEF-233** Mark done / mark blocked with note, reassign and any task lifecycle are not implemented anywhere; there is no *Done* state, so completion is never audited (current SRD FR-OPS-001 label [O] overstated).
- **DEF-234** *+ Operations task* inserts a fixed placeholder with no form, owner, time or title entry; *Calendar* and *Export runbook* only show toasts and *Export runbook* claims "Runbook exported" although nothing is exported.
- **DEF-235** KPI tiles, dependency percentages, link counts and chart series are static and mutually inconsistent: *Due today* 12 vs 7 listed tasks; *Cash deadlines* 3 vs 4 chart events; "US$ 1.6m gross flows" vs 3.18m in the chart; *Settlement exposure* US$ 842k vs the single US$ 412k fail; quick link "6 open" vs sidebar badge 14 vs superseded V33 "14 breaks"; sidebar *Operations Control* badge "4" matches nothing on the page.
- **DEF-236** No action-level permission: auditor, compliance, system_admin and portfolio_manager (read-only in practice) can press *+ Operations task* and *Export runbook*.
- **DEF-237** Six or more inbound links labelled "Reconciliations" / "Reconciliation evidence" route to `operations` instead of `reconciliations`: command-palette item *Reconciliations*, IBOR *Reconcile positions*, 360-drawer *Open reconciliations* and *Reconciliation health*, order-drawer *Reconciliation evidence*, position-layer *Reconciliations →*, accounting-layer *Resolve blockers*.
- **DEF-238** Task detail modal cannot be closed with Esc; no focus trap or initial focus; no keyboard handling for runbook rows (they are `div` elements, not buttons).
- **DEF-239** The filter and any manually added task are lost on reload; no empty-state message; no overdue indication.
- **DEF-240** Dead legacy code on this page key (reconciliation workbench builders, V16 hub strip *Receipt matching / Unit register / Fee engine / Complaints*, and a read of `matanho-recon-v12` in localStorage) targets selectors that no longer exist; it must not be carried into production.
- **DEF-241** Items that depend on another workspace (*Valuation*, *Accounting*) are not hidden or disabled when the user lacks the destination permission.
- FR-OPS-007: Operations task register — create, view, filter, assign, schedule, block, unblock and complete tasks with owner, deadline (CAT), area, dependency and evidence — AC: every transition is an explicit sub-resource call, requires the stated note/evidence, writes an audit event, and the runbook reflects the new state without reload.
- FR-OPS-008: Runbook filters and search — state (*All / Due / Blocked / Scheduled / Done*), owner, area and free-text search with deadline sort — AC: filters combine with AND; the empty state reads "No tasks match this filter."
- FR-OPS-009: Live status panel — KPI tiles, dependency percentages, link counts, workload and cash-deadline charts computed from live task, settlement, cash, valuation and accounting data — AC: figures equal the source workspaces' counts at the same as-of time; changing a source updates the panel within one refresh.
- FR-OPS-010: Task dependency and hand-off — a task may depend on other tasks or controls and hands off to a downstream owner — AC: dependants of an incomplete task cannot be completed; completing a task notifies the next owner and moves cleared dependants from *Blocked* to *Due*.
- FR-OPS-011: Runbook calendar and export — operating-day, month-end, quarter-end and event-driven deadlines in a calendar view, and CSV/XLSX export of the runbook — AC: the export file contains exactly the rows visible under the active filter and records an audit event.
- FR-OPS-012: Add an action-level permission `operations.task.manage` (create, assign, block, complete) for `operations` and `fund_accountant`, keeping `auditor` read-only — AC: users without it see tasks read-only and the task endpoints return 403.
- FR-OPS-013: Chart interactions — tooltips with exact values, click-through from a workload hour or cash event to the filtered tasks — AC: hover shows the value and series name; click filters the runbook.
- Q-70: Is the runbook per fund/portfolio, per business unit, or firm-wide, and are tasks generated automatically from scheduled events (settlement dates, capital-call due dates, election deadlines) or only created manually? — default: firm-wide, mix of system-generated recurring tasks and manual tasks.
- Q-71: Which roles may complete or block a task, and is maker/checker required for control tasks such as *Prepare NAV close readiness*? — default: `operations` and `fund_accountant` may create/complete; control tasks require a different completer than the creator.
- Q-72: Should *Service health* come from `GET /api/health?deep=1`, from the integration registry (5.A.23), or both? — default: both, as the lowest of the two.
- Q-73: Operating-day hours and cut-offs (the workload chart spans 09:00-18:00 CAT; tasks run 15:50-17:30) — are they configurable per calendar and holiday set? — default: configurable operating window 08:00-18:00 CAT, ZSE/VFEX holiday calendar.

No bridge script, no `/v1/recon/*` route, no Prisma model and no `localStorage` use exists for the final page. The endpoints in the target design are **[I]**: `GET/POST /api/v1/recon/runs`, `GET/PATCH /api/v1/recon/breaks`, `POST /api/v1/recon/breaks/{id}/{assign\|resolve\|accept-match\|query-source}`, `GET/POST /api/v1/recon/sources`, `GET/POST /api/v1/recon/imports`, `POST /api/v1/recon/signoffs`. |
| Entry points | **[O]** Sidebar item *Reconciliations* (icon `#i-ops`, static badge *14*, role-primary for Investment Director, Dealer, Operations, Fund Accountant, Auditor; secondary, shown only under *All workspaces*, for Portfolio Manager, Compliance and System Administrator). **[O]** Operations page link *Open Reconciliations* and the settlement dependency tile (see 5.A.16). **[O-hidden]** Orders page *Open reconciliation* button (hidden by CSS). **[O-superseded]** Order modal *Open post-trade reconciliation*. **[O defect]** Command page *Reconciliations →*, command-palette entry *Reconciliations*, and IBOR *Reconcile positions* all open **Operations**, not this page. |
| Exit points | **[O]** Only the sidebar and global chrome. The page contains no outbound navigation link. |

##### Layout

1. **[O]** Page header (`.v45-recon-head`): eyebrow *MATCH WHAT MATTERS*, H1 *Reconciliations*, description "Internal books are compared with independently received broker, custodian, bank and administrator records. Work only the exceptions that need a person.", and the action buttons *Source health* and *Run matching*. The button *+ Counterparty source* exists in the DOM but is hidden.
2. **[O]** KPI row: four visible tiles (*Needs action*, *Waiting source*, *Ready checker*, *Close readiness*) in a four-column grid (two columns at 1100 px and below). Two further tiles (*Matched today*, *Sources current*) exist but are hidden.
3. **[O]** Progress bar (`.v46-recon-progress`, injected by v46 after the KPI row): label *Reconciliation flow*, five static steps, a static source summary and the toggle link *View sources* / *Hide sources*.
4. **[O-hidden]** End-to-end control-flow section (9 stage buttons): `display:none`, no route to reveal it.
5. **[O-hidden]** Source hub (`#v45SourceHub`): hidden until *View sources* is pressed; contains an internal-books strip and a grid of counterparty source cards.
6. **[O]** Workbench (`.v45-recon-workbench`, columns 300 px and remaining width): left, the exception queue card (title *Needs attention*, search box, family select, case list); right, the case detail pane.
7. **[O]** Responsive: padding 18 px / 16 px at 900 px and below; the header stacks and the action buttons stretch at 760 px and below; the progress bar scrolls horizontally at 760 px and below; the source grid is three columns, two at 1100 px and below.
8. **[O]** Overlays: the v45 modal (`#v45Modal` with `#v45Backdrop`, z-index 421, width `min(860px, 100vw - 28px)`) and the global toast stack. No drawer is used.

**Case detail pane (final DOM)** [O], in order:

1. **Head**: kicker `{id} · {family}`; H2 case title; chip showing the group text. The paragraph "Start with the two records and their lineage, then decide whether this is a real break." is removed by v46. Chip colour: *Waiting source* amber (warn), *Ready checker* blue (info), status *Closed* green (good), every other group red (bad).
2. **Banner**: eyebrow *WHY THIS IS HERE*, H2 = the case `why` text, paragraph = the case `next` text; amount box showing the `difference` and "{confidence}% match confidence", or "Source not present" when confidence is 0.
3. **Compare row** (three columns: internal, 108 px difference box, external):
   - **Internal card** *INTERNAL EXPECTED RECORD*: bold value, line `{label} · {ref}`, button *View internal source record*. Lineage block (hidden until *Show evidence*): *Origin* (provider), *Transport*, *Record* (raw record string), *Received / as-of*.
   - **Difference card**: caption *DIFFERENCE*, or *MATCHED* when the case status is *Closed*; the difference value; "{confidence}% confidence", or "Awaiting source" when confidence is 0.
   - **External card** *INDEPENDENT COUNTERPARTY RECORD*: bold value, line `{label} · {ref}`, button *Preview counterparty record*. Lineage block (hidden until *Show evidence*): *Provider*, *How received*, *Artifact / msg*, *Received*.
4. **Match explanation** (hidden until *Show evidence*): panel *Matching keys and tolerance* with one tile per key (key name, rule, result), and an aside *NEXT HUMAN ACTION* showing the first sentence of `next` in bold plus the full `next` text.
5. **Action row** (`.v45-case-actions`): the v46 toggle *Show evidence* / *Hide evidence*, then the buttons in the Actions table.

##### States

- **Empty:** **[O]** Queue with no matching case: "No cases in this view." The detail pane is not cleared (it keeps the last selected case). Registered sources with no population show latest "No records yet", records 0 and control total "Awaiting first source" (Source health modal only).
- **Loading:** **[O]** None. Every action is synchronous; there is no spinner, no skeleton and no disabled-while-running state.
- **Error:** **[O]** Only the toasts "Source unavailable" (error), "Matching gated" (warn), and the browser's native required-field bubbles in *Register reconciliation source*. **[I]** No network error state exists because no network call exists.
- **Disabled / read-only:** **[O]** No control on the page is ever disabled. Hidden by CSS: *+ Counterparty source*, KPIs *Matched today* and *Sources current*, the control-flow section, the lineage blocks and the match-explanation panel (until *Show evidence*), the source hub (until *View sources*), source-card *Frequency* and *Population* cells, the source-card transport paragraph, and the case action *Open source hub*. Read-only: the six inputs in the Source preview modal.
- **Conditional:** **[O]** The primary case button depends on the group (*Fetch missing source*, *Submit maker resolution*, *Checker approve & close*, none for *Closed*). The group chip colour depends on the group and status. The *Difference* card caption becomes *MATCHED* only when the status is *Closed*. The confidence text becomes "Source not present" or "Awaiting source" when confidence is 0. *Close readiness* is *Conditional* while any case has severity `critical`. The *Run matching* gate depends on the status of every source.

##### Business rules & calculations

- **[O] Final-UI resolution.** The page is rendered several times at boot (static V33 markup, then V33, V34, V35, V36, V44 rebuilds). The v45 rebuild at about 3.6 s after boot is final; v46 then relabels and hides parts of it and re-applies itself 80 ms after every DOM mutation inside the page.
- **[O] Missing source is not a break.** A case whose counterparty population is absent sits in the group *Waiting source* with difference "Not classifiable" and confidence 0; it is counted in *Waiting source*, not in *Needs action*. BR-065: a reconciliation case may not be classified as a break until the independent counterparty population has been received and validated.
- **[O] Run-matching gate.** *Run matching* requires every source (internal and counterparty) to have status `Current`. The case-level *Re-run match* requires only the case's external source to be `Current`.
- **[O] Confidence floor.** *Run matching* raises confidence to at least 94 for non-checker, non-matched cases; *Re-run match* raises it to at least 96. Confidence is never computed from data.
- **[O] State machine (final UI).**
  - *Waiting source* → (*Fetch missing source*) → *Needs action*, status *Source received*, severity `high`.
  - *Needs action* → (*Submit maker resolution*) → *Ready checker*, status *Pending checker*, severity `ready`.
  - *Ready checker* → (*Checker approve & close*) → *Matched*, status *Closed*, severity `matched`, difference "0", confidence 100. Terminal; the case stays listed.
  - There is no reject / return path, no reopen (except the order synchronisation below), no escalation, no assignment, no *Awaiting counterparty* state and no *Overdue* flag.
- **[O] KPI formulas.** *Needs action* = number of cases with group *Needs action*; *Waiting source* = group *Waiting source*; *Ready checker* = group *Ready checker*; *Matched today* = constant 142; *Sources current* = `{counterparty sources with status Current}/{counterparty sources}`; *Close readiness* = *Conditional* if any case has severity `critical`, else *Ready*. There is no match-rate formula in any layer; the 98.74% shown in the superseded static markup is a literal.
- **[O] Tolerance constants (display only, not enforced).** Price 0.5% (trade case); amount 0.01 (cash case); as-of "Within 5 min" (holdings case); NAV "Material threshold"; quantity, order reference, security, settlement date, account, value date, currency "Exact".
- **[O] Control-flow stages** (the section is hidden; initial active stage index 5, so stages 01 to 05 are *done* and 06 is *active*):

  | # | Stage | Short description | Long text |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 1 | *Cut-off* | "Freeze internal books and control scope." | "Freeze the internal OMS, IBOR, ABOR, unit register and valuation population for the agreed business cut-off. Preserve version and as-of time." |
  | 2 | *Acquire* | "Receive broker, custodian, bank, TA and admin records." | "Ingest independent broker, custodian, bank, transfer-agent and administrator populations through registered FIX, API, SFTP, ISO 20022/SWIFT or controlled upload channels." |
  | 3 | *Validate* | "Schema, completeness, duplicates, sequence and timestamps." | "Reject incomplete, duplicate, malformed or out-of-window records before they can create false breaks. Validate schema, sequence, timestamps and required identifiers." |
  | 4 | *Control totals* | "Counts, cash totals, position totals and file/message integrity." | "Prove population completeness using record counts, cash totals, quantity totals, file hashes/checksums and expected delivery schedules." |
  | 5 | *Normalise* | "Map IDs, currencies, dates, instruments and accounts." | "Map external identifiers to internal security, account, portfolio, currency and date keys while retaining the original source record untouched." |
  | 6 | *Match* | "Apply deterministic keys, tolerance and candidate scoring." | "Run exact and tolerant rules. Matched items disappear from human work; low-confidence candidates are retained with explainable matching scores." |
  | 7 | *Investigate* | "Only genuine differences enter the human queue." | "A person investigates only a proven difference. Source lineage, raw record, matching keys and recommended action sit together." |
  | 8 | *Correct & re-match* | "Fix the source system, retain evidence, run the rule again." | "The maker corrects the system of record or obtains counterparty correction, attaches evidence, and re-runs the exact matching rule." |
  | 9 | *Checker & archive* | "Independent sign-off; freeze match evidence for close." | "An independent checker approves the result. Source artifacts, mappings, match result, maker action and checker sign-off are frozen for audit and close." |

  The section header reads *END-TO-END CONTROL FLOW* / "What happens before a break reaches a person" / "Click a stage to see its purpose. A missing source is kept separate from a genuine difference." with the chip "9 controlled stages".
- **[O] Owner and role vocabulary.** The seeded owners are T. Moyo, N. Dube, Client Operations and Fund Accounting. The superseded V33 ribbon names the roles *Operations resolver* (maker) and *Independent operations approver* (checker); no code assigns either role.
- **[O] Order-lifecycle linkage.** On the Orders page the v45 lifecycle shell holds an order (initially ORD-49217, INN, Buy 7,800 @ USD 1.12, portfolio USD Growth, broker Morgan & Co, stage index 5 *Execute*). When the user advances the order to stage index 8 (*Reconcile*) the code:
  1. updates the sample records of *SRC-BRK-FIX* (from stage 4: latest `ACK-{order id}`), *SRC-BRK-NOTE* (from stage 5: latest `CN_{order id}.csv`) and *SRC-CUS-SET* (from stage 7: latest `SET-{order id}`, status `SETTLED` from stage 8);
  2. **overwrites the first case in the list (REC-TRD-49217), whatever its state**: id `REC-{order id}`, title `{ticker} · {order id}`, amount and difference `{currency} {quantity × 0.01 to 2 decimals}` (for the seed "USD 78.00"), internal value "{qty} @ {currency} {price to 2 decimals}", external value "{qty} @ {currency} {price + 0.01 to 2 decimals}", group *Needs action*, status *Investigating*, severity `critical`, confidence 88, new `why` "The independently received broker execution differs from the OMS execution price." and `next` "Open the broker FIX execution and contract note, confirm the economics, then correct the OMS execution or query the broker."; selects the case;
  3. rebuilds the reconciliation page.

  BR-066: the prototype assumes the broker price is always the instruction price plus 0.01, so a trade break is always created at stage 8; production must create a break only when a real difference exists.
- **[O] Orders-page controls that touch this page.** *Open reconciliation* (shown from stage 7, hidden by CSS) navigates to this page and rebuilds it 120 ms later; *Reset demo* (hidden by CSS) restores the order to stage 5 but does not restore the reconciliation case.
- **[O] Persistence.** None for the final UI. Related but unused keys: `matanho-v53-counterpart-imports` (never-attached hub), `matanho-recon-v12` (Operations page workbench, 5.A.16), `matanho-v61-custodian-submissions` (custodian portal, see below).
- **[O] No audit trail.** Copy repeatedly states that evidence is "frozen for audit"; no audit event is emitted.

##### Edge cases

- **[O] Page disappears after a forced rebuild.** The rebuild sets the page class to `page v45-recon`, dropping `active`. The page is visible only while it has `active`, which only `navigate()` adds. *Fetch now*, *Refresh all*, *Save source*, *Fetch missing source* and a flow-stage click therefore blank the workspace until the user clicks the sidebar item again. The same rebuild resets the v46 toggles to *View sources* and *Show evidence* (hub and evidence hidden).
- **[O] Boot glitch.** The v36 rebuild sets `page active v33-workspace`, so between about 1.85 s and 3.25 s after boot the reconciliation page is displayed together with the page the user is on.
- **[O] Endless re-application.** The v46 observer re-applies its relabelling 80 ms after every mutation inside the page, and each application writes text into observed nodes, so the loop runs continuously (about 12 times per second).
- **[O] Search leaves the detail stale.** Typing in the search box re-renders only the queue. If the selected case is filtered out, the queue highlights the first remaining row while the detail pane still shows the previous case. With zero matches the detail keeps the last selected case.
- **[O] Closed cases remain in the queue** with the default amber dot, and the family select has no status filter, although the description says routine matches "disappear".
- **[O] Registering a source blocks matching** until reload: the new source has no kind (so it is not shown in the hub or counted in *Sources current*), its status is *Configured* (so *Refresh all* skips it) and the *Run matching* gate fails on any source that is not `Current`. It cannot be fetched (no card, so no *Fetch now* button).
- **[O] *Refresh all* marks *SRC-TA* `Current`** while it still has 0 records and "Not received", and the *REC-UNITS-TA* case stays *Waiting source*; *Run matching* then passes its gate.
- **[O] *Close readiness* becomes *Ready*** as soon as no case has severity `critical`, including when the two critical cases are merely *Pending checker* (severity `ready`) and while *SRC-TA* is still missing.
- **[O] Sample-data lineage.** *REC-UNITS-TA* and *REC-NAV-GEIV* name `SRC-OMS` as their internal source, so their lineage shows "Matanho OMS / Internal API / event bus"; no unit-register or valuation-book source exists.
- **[O] Static counts disagree.** Sidebar badge *14*, Operations link "14 breaks →" or "6 open →", and the live *Needs action* value 4 are independent.
- **[O] Fetch for the Units case** sets the case external value to the source control total "312 investor-unit rows", which is a count, not a comparable unit total.

##### Gaps, defects & open questions

- **DEF-242** Forced rebuilds (*Fetch now*, *Refresh all*, *Save source*, *Fetch missing source*) hide the page because the `active` class is lost.
- **DEF-243** The v46 re-application loop never stops and also triggers the body-wide V53 observer.
- **DEF-244** The v36 rebuild shows the page stacked over another page for about 1.4 s at boot.
- **DEF-245** A source registered through the form has no kind, is invisible in the hub, never reaches `Current` and permanently gates *Run matching* until reload.
- **DEF-246** *Refresh all* marks a never-received source `Current`.
- **DEF-247** Maker resolution requires no rationale, no evidence reference, no root cause and no prior match; checker approval has no maker ≠ checker test and no role or permission test; the read-only Auditor can act.
- **DEF-248** *Close readiness* ignores pending-checker items and missing sources.
- **DEF-249** *Matched today* (142) and the sidebar badge (14) are constants.
- **DEF-250** The toast helper writes its message as HTML, and the registered provider name is inserted unescaped into the "Source registered" toast (HTML injection).
- **DEF-251** The v45 modal does not close on Escape and does not trap focus; the search box has no label.
- **DEF-252** Order stage 8 overwrites and reopens the first case regardless of its state and does not update its keys list.
- **DEF-253** Command-page *Reconciliations →*, the command-palette *Reconciliations* entry and IBOR *Reconcile positions* navigate to Operations.
- **DEF-254** The seeded Units and NAV cases use the OMS as their internal source.
- FR-REC-002: Provide a persisted reconciliation engine (runs, breaks, sources, imports, sign-offs) behind the `/api/v1/recon/*` endpoints — AC: a run for a family and as-of date creates one break per unmatched or out-of-tolerance item, matched items create no queue entry, and a run record stores matched count and break count.
- FR-REC-003: Compute every KPI from persisted data, including a match rate = matched items ÷ total items in the run population, expressed as a percentage with two decimals — AC: the value equals the ratio of the run statistics for the selected as-of date and family.
- FR-REC-004: Maker resolution must require a cause, a rationale and at least one evidence reference — AC: the *Submit maker resolution* request is rejected with a validation error when any of the three is missing.
- FR-REC-005: Checker approval must be refused when the approver equals the maker (BR-001) and must require a distinct permission — AC: the same user receives a "Segregation of duties" error; a user without the checker permission cannot see the button.
- FR-REC-006: Add *Assign*, *Attach evidence*, *Accept candidate match*, *Query source*, *Escalate* and *Return to maker* actions with audit events — AC: each action records user, time and reason and appears in the case history.
- FR-REC-007: Add a *Daily sign-off* per family and as-of date, blocked while any Critical or High break is open or any scheduled source is missing — AC: the sign-off is recorded with the checker identity and freezes the evidence population.
- FR-REC-008: Keep closed and matched cases out of the default queue and provide a status filter — AC: the default list contains no case with status *Closed*.
- FR-REC-009: Show a running state for long-running actions (*Run matching*, *Fetch now*) — AC: the button is disabled with a progress indicator until the job completes and an error toast is shown on failure.
- FR-REC-010: Close modals on Escape and trap focus; label the search input — AC: Escape closes the modal and focus returns to the opener.
- BR-067: Quantity and order-reference matching are exact; price tolerance, amount tolerance, as-of tolerance and NAV materiality are effective-dated configuration per family, not constants in code.
- Q-74: Is a missing counterparty record a break (V61 wording) or a source-completeness exception that blocks matching (V56 behaviour)? — default: a source-completeness exception that blocks matching and daily sign-off, shown separately from value breaks.
- Q-75: Which permission codes gate resolve, approve, sign-off and source management? — default: reuse `operations.view` plus maker ≠ checker until `recon.signoff` is approved (Q-04).
- Q-76: Which families are in scope for the first release? — default: the six families present in the running UI (Trades, Settlement, Cash, Holdings, Units, Pricing / NAV); the other six V33 families are deferred.
- Q-77: Where do the unit register and valuation book appear as internal sources? — default: add internal sources `SRC-UNITS` and `SRC-VAL`.

##### V61 changes (documented, not in running UI)

Source: `legacy-static/v65/V61_CHANGES.md`. The V65 admin `index.html` and the V61 admin scripts are not in the repository (the V65 manifest lists them); the running admin UI is still V56.

| # | V61 behaviour | Running V56 difference | Label |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Reconciliations "starts with the practical question: how will the independent counterpart record reach Matanho?" and offers three operating routes. | V56 opens on the work queue; sources are behind *View sources*. | [V61] |
| 2 | **Route 1, broker / counterparty API or connector.** Configure provider, endpoint, transport and authentication method; supports REST API, FIX adapter and SFTP-style models; *Test* and *refresh* controls in the reconciliation workspace; the browser stores only non-secret routing metadata and production credentials live in a server-side connector or secrets vault. | V56 *Register reconciliation source* captures provider, role, channel, schedule, endpoint, authentication and schema; there is no *Test* control; the entry is in memory only, is invisible in the hub and blocks *Run matching*. *Fetch now* and *Refresh all* are the only refresh controls. | [V61] |
| 3 | **Route 2, manual controlled file import.** CSV, TXT, JSON, XML, XLS/XLSX and PDF can be staged; CSV and JSON execution data is normalised into reconciliation records where possible; the importer recognises ClOrdID, ExecID, Symbol, Side, LastQty, LastPx and SettlDate; every import creates a batch record with source, account, filename, record count and import time. | V56 has no reachable upload. The never-attached V53 hub accepts CSV, TXT, JSON, XML and PDF (no XLS/XLSX), counts lines, does no field recognition or normalisation and has no account field. | [V61] |
| 4 | **Route 3, custodian / counterparty portal** (`custodian-portal.html`): the counterparty enters executed trades during the day and later submits official day-end cash, holdings and trade-control totals with an uploaded official file and SHA-256 fingerprint; submissions are available to the manager's reconciliation staging area on the same deployment origin. | V56 has no staging area and nothing reads portal submissions (see next sub-section). | [V61] |
| 5 | Four stages: **Source records → Run matching → Resolve exceptions → Sign-off**. | V56 shows a static five-step bar (*Sources*, *Validate*, *Match*, *Resolve*, *Close*); the nine-stage flow is hidden. | [V61] |
| 6 | Internal book records are compared with independent counterpart records; exact trade reference is preferred; ticker, side and quantity provide a secondary match. | V56 has no matching algorithm; keys are static display strings per case. | [V61] |
| 7 | Quantity must match exactly and the execution-price tolerance is ±0.01 in the prototype. | V56 displays a 0.5% price tolerance (relative) for the trade case and 0.01 for the cash amount. | [V61] |
| 8 | Routine matches disappear from the exception queue. | V56 keeps *Closed* / *Matched* cases in the queue. | [V61] |
| 9 | Missing counterpart records and genuine differences create exceptions. | V56 deliberately does not treat a missing source as a break (*Waiting source*, "Not classifiable"). | [V61] |
| 10 | Material exceptions block daily sign-off. | V56 has no daily sign-off; only the *Close readiness* KPI (V33 had a blocking sign-off toast). | [V61] |
| 11 | Resolution requires a maker rationale and an evidence reference. | V56 *Submit maker resolution* requires neither (V33 required a rationale only). | [V61] |
| 12 | Daily sign-off records an independent checker confirmation. | V56 has no sign-off record and no maker ≠ checker check. | [V61] |

##### Custodian portal feed (V65)

Source: `legacy-static/v65/custodian-portal.html`, ported as the Next.js app `portals/custodian-web` (port 3104) with a lightly modified inline script. Nothing in the V56 admin portal consumes it.

- **[V61] Page.** Title "Matanho Custodian Data Portal"; brand *matanho* with *CUSTODIAN DATA PORTAL*; badge "Controlled counterparty workspace · Demo"; hero eyebrow *TRADE CONFIRMATION · DAY-END BOOK · RECONCILIATION EVIDENCE*, H1 "Custodian / Counterparty Portal", description "Enter the executed trade as soon as it is available, then submit the independent day-end book later. The asset manager receives both records in the same reconciliation staging area."; three steps *01 · EXECUTION* "Record the trade after execution", *02 · DAY END* "Submit cash, holdings and trade control totals", *03 · RECONCILE* "Matanho matches against its internal book".
- **[V61] Channel and storage.** `localStorage` key `matanho-v61-custodian-submissions` holding `{executions: [...], dayEnd: [...]}`; in-memory fallback when `localStorage` is unavailable; a `storage` event re-renders another open tab. No API, no BroadcastChannel, no postMessage. Compared with V56: no admin code reads this key; the admin portal (port 3100) and the custodian portal (port 3104) are different origins, so even a reader could not see the data.
- **[V61] Tab *Trade execution* (`#tradeForm`)**, record appended to `executions`:

| Field | Control | Required | Options / default / placeholder | Validation today (code) | Target validation | Error message |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Trade reference* | Text | Yes | Default `TRD-260904-201`; stored trimmed as `ref` | HTML `required`; script falsy check | Unique per custodian and account | "Incomplete trade" / "Complete all required execution fields." |
| *Execution time* | datetime-local | Yes | Default current local time; stored as `executionTime` | HTML `required` | Not in the future | Browser default |
| *Account / portfolio* | Text | Yes | Default `BGF-001` | HTML `required`; script falsy check | Must exist in the account catalogue | "Incomplete trade" / "Complete all required execution fields." |
| *Security / ticker* | Text | Yes | Default `DLTA.ZW`; stored upper-cased | HTML `required`; script falsy check | Must exist in the security master | "Incomplete trade" / "Complete all required execution fields." |
| *Side* | Select | Yes | *BUY* (default), *SELL* | None | Same | None |
| *Quantity* | Number, min 1 | Yes | Default 10000; stored as a number | HTML `required` and `min 1`; script falsy check | Positive integer | "Incomplete trade" / "Complete all required execution fields." |
| *Execution price* | Number, step 0.0001 | Yes | Default 0.184; stored as a number | HTML `required`; script falsy check | Positive, 4 decimals | "Incomplete trade" / "Complete all required execution fields." |
| *Currency* | Select | Yes | *USD* (default), *ZWG* | None | Same | None |
| *Settlement date* | date | Yes | Default today + 2 days | HTML `required` | Not before the execution date | Browser default |
| *Executing broker* | Text | Yes | Default `IH Securities` | HTML `required` | Approved-broker list | Browser default |
| *Execution note* | Textarea | No | Placeholder "Optional market, allocation or settlement note" | None | Maximum length | None |

  Actions: *Clear* (reset; blanks the computed date defaults), *Submit execution* (adds `id` "EXEC-" + timestamp, `created` in the format "dd Mon yyyy, HH:mm", status `Submitted`; toast "Execution submitted" / "{ref} is available to Matanho Reconciliations."; resets the form and re-applies defaults). Note under the form: "The portal creates an immutable submission record in this prototype. Production access would be authenticated, permissioned and signed by the custodian user."
- **[V61] Tab *Day-end package* (`#dayForm`)**, record appended to `dayEnd`:

| Field | Control | Required | Options / default / placeholder | Validation today (code) | Target validation | Error message |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Statement date* | date | Yes | Default today; stored as `date` | HTML `required`; script check | Business day | "Incomplete package" / "Statement date and account are required." |
| *Account* | Text | Yes | Default `BGF-001` | HTML `required`; script check | Must exist in the account catalogue | "Incomplete package" / "Statement date and account are required." |
| *Closing cash* | Number, step 0.01 | Yes | Default 6320000 | HTML `required` | Matches the file control total | Browser default |
| *Currency* | Select | Yes | *USD* (default), *ZWG* | None | Same | None |
| *Holdings market value* | Number, step 0.01 | Yes | Default 21839000 | HTML `required` | Matches the file control total | Browser default |
| *Trades in day-end book* | Number, min 0 | Yes | Default 3 | HTML `required`, `min 0` | Equals the number of executions submitted for the day | Browser default |
| *Official day-end file* | File | No | Accepts `.csv`, `.xlsx`, `.xls`, `.xml`, `.json`, `.pdf`, `.txt`; label "Select holdings / cash / settlement file" with the note "Filename and SHA-256 fingerprint are recorded when supported" | None | Required for an official package; size limit; malware scan | None |
| *Control note* | Textarea | No | Default "Official day-end balances approved for reconciliation." | None | Maximum length | None |

  Actions: *Clear*; *Submit day-end package* (adds `id` "DAY-" + timestamp, `file` name, `size`, `sha256` (hex digest through `crypto.subtle`, empty string when unsupported or no file), `created`, status `Submitted`; toast "Day-end package submitted" / "{account} is ready for reconciliation."). **File contents are not stored**, only name, size and hash.
- **[V61] Status panel.** Heading "Submission status", text "Records entered here become available to the manager's Reconciliations workspace."; metric tiles *Executions* and *Day-end packs* (counts); activity list of the newest eight entries ("Execution · {ref}" with "{side} {qty} {ticker} @ {price}", or "Day-end · {account}" with "Cash {currency} {cash} · {trades} trades", each with the pill *Submitted* and the created time); empty state "No submissions yet" / "Enter the first execution or day-end package."
- **[V61] What the admin staging area would read.** The same-origin key `matanho-v61-custodian-submissions`; executions matchable on `ref`, or on ticker, side and quantity with the ±0.01 price tolerance; day-end control totals (cash, holdings value, trade count) per account and statement date.
- **[V61] Compared with V56.** None of this is consumed by the admin portal. FR-REC-011: Replace the browser-storage hand-off with a server-side staging channel — AC: a custodian submission made on the custodian portal is visible to the reconciliation staging area of the admin portal after authentication, with the submitting user, timestamp and file hash stored.
- **DEF-255** The custodian portal sorts activity by a string compare of the formatted date, which is not chronological across months; *Clear* blanks the date and time defaults; there is no authentication, no maker/checker step and no signing.
- **DEF-256** Cross-portal hand-off through `localStorage` cannot work across ports 3100 and 3104 (see SRD 13.4).

#### 5.A.18 NAV & Valuation (`valuation`, `valuation.view`)

| Attribute | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Daily per-fund NAV control: confirm source evidence, resolve the material valuation exception, submit maker review, then release NAV through an independent checker. **[O]** (final-UI subtitle: "One daily control: confirm source evidence, resolve only material exceptions, then complete maker/checker release.") |
| Access | Page gate `valuation.view` (the same permission also gates `accounting`). Roles holding it in the default role map: `investment_director`, `portfolio_manager`, `compliance`, `operations`, `fund_accountant`, `auditor`, `system_admin` **[O]**. Roles without it: `dealer`, `analyst`, `client_services` **[O]**. Without it the sidebar item is hidden (`hidden-by-rbac`); opening the page programmatically shows the error toast "Access restricted" / "`<Role>` does not have permission to open this workspace."; if the current page becomes disallowed after a role change, the shell redirects to the first visible nav item **[O]**. No control on the page carries a per-action permission (see Gaps). The capability matrix row *Run NAV / valuations* lists only `fund_accountant`, but it is display-only **[O]**. |
| Prototype layer | `v49-enhancements.js` (`renderNav49`) replaces the whole `#page-valuation` innerHTML about 3.8 s after load and is the **final UI** **[O]**. Superseded, do not specify: static markup `23-page-valuation.html` (V33 design, also in `legacy-static/index.html`) and `v33-rebuild.js` (`renderNav`/`initNav`). Dead code that targets non-existent elements/actions: `01-inline.js` actions `price-exceptions`, `start-nav-run`, `review-valuation-evidence`, and `02-v7-institutional-enhancement-js.js` `startNavRunV9`. No layer v50–v56 touches this page. |
| Wiring status | **Prototype** for every data element and action. No `/v1/nav/*` endpoint exists in the backend (modules present: admin, clients, company, documents, files, identity, investor, kyc, notifications) and no legacy-bridge file reads or writes NAV or valuation data **[O]**. All state lives in an in-memory object (`navState`) and is lost on reload; no `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`/IndexedDB key is used **[O]**. The access-policy field `navApproval` (`independent` \| `dual`) is bridged to the admin API (admin policies endpoint, stored with `bankApproval`) but is **never read** by this page **[O]**. The only persisted valuation-related model is `InvestorSnapshot` (investor-portal snapshot with Draft/Published/Superseded and maker/checker ids), unrelated to this page **[O]**. Target endpoints **[P]**: `GET/POST /api/v1/nav/runs`, `POST /api/v1/nav/runs/{id}/{recalculate\|maker-review\|release}`, `PATCH /api/v1/nav/runs/{id}/exceptions/{exId}` (already listed in section 11.3), plus a new evidence-document upload and a NAV-pack render endpoint (see Gaps). |
| Entry points | (1) Sidebar item *NAV & Valuation* (relabelled *NAV & valuation* by the v16 focus script; primary nav for `operations` and `fund_accountant`, secondary (visible only after *All workspaces*) for the other permitted roles) **[O]**. (2) Operations Control: dependency tile *Valuation* ("72% ready", "1 private price exception") and quick link *Open NAV & Valuation* ("Resolve pricing and release NAV", "1 blocker →") **[O]**. (3) Command / dashboard: control-queue button *Valuation* ("1", "Material price review"), today-strip item *NAV / valuation* ("1 blocker", "Independent price evidence"), risk row *Private valuation evidence stale* ("Growth Equity IV · release impact") **[O]**. (4) Accounting & Close second layer: header button *Valuation* and list item *Price approval evidence* ("Hierarchy, overrides and reviewers") **[O]**. (5) Clicking the sidebar item re-renders the page 80 ms later, resetting nothing (state is retained) **[O]**. (6) Dashboard items *Resolve private valuation exception* and *Valuation release exception* are wired to a non-existent layer `valuation-exception` and open the generic work-queue layer instead of this page **[O]** (DEFECT, see Gaps). |
